info.title: Neon Workspace API
info.description:
The HTTP API of Neon Workspace.

Every error response has the same body: `{"error": {"code": string, "message": string}}`. `code` is stable and meant for programs, such as `not_found` or `invalid_json`; `message` says what went wrong, for people. A request with several wrong fields, such as settings, also lists each in `problems`. A rate-limited request answers 429 with `Retry-After`.

A request authenticates with the session cookie that `POST /api/v1/auth/login` sets, or with `Authorization: Bearer nw_…`, an API token. A token's scopes decide what it may do: `read` for safe methods, `write` for the others, `admin` for `/api/v1/admin`. A request that changes something and carries no `Authorization` header must come from the server's own origin: its `Origin`, or else its `Referer`, must match the public URL.

get.description: Needs a session or an API token with the read scope.

patch.description: Needs a session or an API token with the write scope.

post.description: Needs the current password and a browser session; API tokens cannot. Signs out every other session, and mails the account that its password changed.

401.description: unauthenticated, or invalid_credentials: the current password is wrong.

get.summary: The web app's look for this user
get.description: Defaults for what the user never set. Needs a session or an API token with the read scope.

put.summary: Save the web app's look for this user
put.description: Replaces all four. Needs a session or an API token with the write scope.

get.description: Needs a session or an API token with the read scope.

200.description: The sessions that have not expired.

delete.description: Ends every session of the user but the current one. Only from a browser session.
Ends one of the user's sessions; ending the current one also clears its cookie. Only from a browser session.

get.description: Needs a session or an API token with the read scope.

post.description: Its secret is in this answer only; the server keeps its hash. A token never does more than its owner's role allows. Only from a browser session.

403.description: forbidden: not a browser session, or the admin scope for a user who is no admin.

delete.description: It stops working at once. Only from a browser session.

get.description: Each invite with who signed up with it. Codes are not listed: copy one with `GET /admin/invites/{id}/code`.

post.description: With an address, mails the invite there, naming the admin: the mail is queued with the invite, and `queued` is true.

409.description: invite_code_taken, or email_taken: the address has an account.

post.summary: Check a code as it is typed

get.description: Opens the code's sealed copy, which is kept while a secret key is configured.

409.description: code_unavailable: it was not kept, or its key is gone.

post.description: It admits no more sign-ups, and stays listed.

get.description: Only confirmed requests: an address must open its mailed link first.

post.description: Makes an invite bound to the request's address, for one sign-up, and mails it there, the mail queued with the invite. While mail is not set up the invite is made all the same, `queued` is false, and the code can be handed over.

404.description: not_found: no such request, or it is not waiting.

409.description: email_taken: the address has an account.

post.description: The address may ask again in 30 days, and is told so by mail while `auth.request_denied_mail` is on and mail is set up.

404.description: not_found: no such request, or it is not waiting.

get.description: Every setting with its value, default and where the value comes from.

patch.description: Applies the changes together, at once and without a restart, or none of them: every value is checked, then the rules across settings. Settings pinned by the environment or the config file cannot change here. Secret settings need `secrets.keys`, as they are kept encrypted.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Accounts on the page, 1 to 200; 50 when absent.

post.description: Works whatever the registration mode, closed included. The address counts as verified.

patch.summary: Change an account's role, disable or enable it, or verify its address
patch.description: Changes only what the body names. The last admin who can sign in can be neither demoted nor disabled.

post.summary: Mail an account its verification link again

204.description: The link was made and its mail queued.

429.description: rate_limited: one a minute, five a day.

get.description: Which forms to show: the registration mode, and whether verification, password reset and requests to join are on, which also needs mail set up.

post.description: Says whether an invite admits sign-ups now, and the address it is bound to.

400.description: invalid_invite: used up, expired, revoked or none.

post.description: Mails the address a link to confirm the request; admins see it once it is confirmed. Answers the same whatever comes of it, so it tells nobody which addresses have accounts or requests.
Takes the token of the mailed link. The admins see the request from now.

400.description: invalid_link: used already, or too old.

post.description: Opens a browser session and sets its cookie: `neon_session`, or `__Host-neon_session` when the server's public URL is https; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Secure over https. An unknown address and a wrong password answer the same, and take as long; a disabled or unverified account is only told so after the right password.
Ends the current browser session and clears its cookie. With an API token, it ends nothing: revoke the token instead.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset link
post.description: Mails a link setting a new password to the account of the address, if it has one. Answers the same whether it has one or not.

post.summary: Set a new password with a mailed link
post.description: The link works once. It verifies the address and signs the account out of every session, but signs nobody in.
Signs up as the registration mode allows: anyone while it is open, with an invite while it is by invite, nobody while it is closed. Signs nobody in.
Mails a new link to the account of the address if it must still verify. Answers the same whether it has one or not.
Takes the token of the link mailed after signing up. The link works once. It signs nobody in: the password is still needed.

400.description: invalid_link: used already, or too old.

get.description: The instance's name and the server's version. Needs no authentication, so clients can check they reached a Neon server.

ApiToken.description: An API token, without its secret.

expires_at.description: Absent for a token that never expires.

prefix.description: The token's first characters, to recognise it.

AuthConfig.description: Which sign-in and sign-up forms are on, and what a password needs.

password_reset.description: Forgotten passwords can be reset by mail.

requests.description: People without an invite can ask for one.

verify_email.description: Self sign-ups verify their address by a mailed link before they sign in.

CodeRequest.description:
The body of routes that take an invite code. It goes in the body, out of URLs and
their logs.

expires_at.description: After now; absent for a token that never expires.

scopes.description: At least one; admin only for an admin.

code.description:
8 to 64 letters, digits, `-` and `_`, matched whatever their case; made by the
server when absent.

email.description:
Mails the invite there; only that address signs up with it, once. The server makes
its code and its end, so it takes none of the fields below.

expires_at.description: After now and within a year; `auth.invite_ttl` from now when absent.

CreatedApiToken.description: A new token with its secret, shown this once.

CreatedInvite.description:
A new invite with its code. The code is shown here, and again only from its sealed
copy when a secret key is configured.

queued.description:
For an invite meant to be mailed: whether its mail was queued, with the invite. It
is not while mail is not set up; the code can be handed over instead. Delivery
shows in the mail status of `GET /admin/settings`.

CredentialKind.description: How a request proved who it is.

EmailRequest.description: An address, for the forms that answer the same whatever it is.

code.description: Stable and meant for programs, such as `not_found` or `invalid_json`.

problems.description: Each field that is wrong and why, when a request had several, such as settings.

code_kept.description: Whether its code can be copied again.

email.description: The address it is bound to, which alone signs up with it; absent for any address.

max_uses.description: How many sign-ups it admits, and how many it did.

signups.description: Who signed up with it, oldest first.

InviteCode.description: An invite's code, to copy again.

InviteCodeCheck.description: What keeps a typed code from making an invite.

problem.description: Its form, or another invite having it; absent when it can make one.

by_email.description: Whether invites can be mailed now: switched on, and mail set up.

InviteLookup.description: What the sign-up form needs to know of an invite.

email.description: The address it is bound to, which the form fills in; absent for any address.

InviteStatus.description: Whether an invite admits sign-ups now, and why not.

user_id.description: The account's id and address, absent once it is gone.

requests.description: Those waiting first, then those decided in the last 30 days.

note.description: For the admins, plain text, at most 500 characters.

JoinStatus.description: Where a request to join is.

scopes.description: A session has every scope its role allows; a token, its own.

Me.description: The signed-in user, and what this request may do.

name.description: The instance's name, from the `instance.name` setting.

Mode.description: Light or dark, or whichever the system prefers.

Preferences.description: The look of the web app, kept with the account.

accent_hue.description: A whole number of degrees, 0 to 359.

key.description: The field, such as a setting's key.

display_name.description: The address's local part when absent.

invite_code.description: Needed while registration is by invite.

must_verify.description:
The account signs in only once it opened the link mailed to it, which was queued
with the account. Another can be asked for with `POST /auth/verification`.

Role.description: What an account may do on the instance.

Scope.description: What an API token may do: `read`, `write`, or the admin pages' work, `admin`.

SessionInfo.description: A browser session of the user.

current.description: The session this request came with.

Setting.description: A runtime setting as admins see it, with secrets redacted.

pinned.description: Set by the environment or the config file, so it cannot change here.

value.description: A secret shows as `[redacted]` when set, and empty when not.

SettingSource.description: Where a setting's value comes from.

SignedIn.description: A new session. Its token is only in the cookie.

absolute_expires_at.description: When it ends however much it is used.

expires_at.description: When the session ends unless it is used before.

TokenRequest.description: The body of routes that take a token from a mailed link.

display_name.description: At most 100 characters; blank takes the address's local part.

changes.description:
By key: the new value, as JSON of the setting's type, or null to go back to the
default.

disabled.description: Disabling signs the account out everywhere.

email_verified.description: True marks the address verified; it cannot be made false.

disabled_at.description: Set while the account is disabled.

email_verified_at.description: Unset while the address must still be verified.

UserPage.description: A page of accounts in the order they were made.

next.description: Pass it as `after` for the next page; absent on the last one.

Verified.description: An address a link verified, for the sign-in form.

api_token.description: An API token, nw_ and 43 characters, made under /api/v1/account/tokens.

session_cookie.name: neon_session
session_cookie.description: The browser session, set by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Named __Host-neon_session when the server's public URL is https.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Signing up, in and out, and the mailed links. Open to anyone.
